documents.title: Guideline: Responsible Use of Generative AI in Academic Work
documents.summary: A provost guideline that welcomes responsible GenAI use but gives instructors complete autonomy and requires every syllabus to carry a policy statement. It supplies three sample statements (open, restricted, prohibited), disclosure templates, student duties on privacy and verification, and lists the university-licensed tools.
documents.stance_why: The guideline says the instructor "has complete autonomy in determining the pedagogical use of GenAI tools" and offers "Option 1: Open Use", "Option 2: Restricted Use" and "Option 3: Prohibited Use" templates, so it sets no single stance and delegates, with tiers listed.

units.why: The Context paragraph says the university "supports the exploration and responsible use GenAI technologies", an institution-level statement of purpose, so P56 (framework) and not P02, because it sets no operational default.
units.anchor: supports the exploration and responsible use GenAI technologies to enhance student learning
units.frag_start: The Florida Institute of Technology recognizes

units.why: "must align with the university's commitment to academic integrity, ethical standards" states a principle binding all GenAI use, so a framework statement (P56).
units.anchor: must align with the university’s commitment to academic integrity, ethical standards

units.why: "recognizes the transformative potential of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in education" gives a reason in favor of AI in education; I chose P44 (AI value as rationale) over P56 because it argues for the worth of AI rather than setting scope.
units.anchor: recognizes the transformative potential of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in education and research
units.frag_start: The Florida Institute of Technology recognizes

units.why: "Students must adhere to specific policies and guidelines set by the course instructor" makes the instructor the rule-setter, so P04 and not P11, which is about non-carryover between courses.
units.anchor: Students must adhere to specific policies and guidelines set by the course instructor

units.why: "Students must consult the course instructor if they are uncertain" before using GenAI is the ask-first rule (P10).
units.anchor: Students must consult the course instructor if they are uncertain

units.why: "without instructor approval" makes unapproved AI use in assignments, tests, projects and reports off limits, which is the default when nothing is approved (P06); the misconduct label is coded in the next unit as P36.
units.anchor: assignments, tests, projects, and reports, without instructor approval

units.why: The same sentence says such use "is considered a violation of academic integrity", classing it as misconduct handled by integrity processes (P36).
units.anchor: is considered a violation of academic integrity

units.why: "students must clearly disclose the use of GenAI tool(s) and their specific contribution" with citations is a disclosure-with-submission duty (P24); P25 not chosen because no tool/prompt details are required here.
units.anchor: students must clearly disclose the use of GenAI tool(s) and their specific contribution

units.why: "Students are fully responsible for the ethical use of GenAI and the appropriateness, accuracy and originality of their work" makes students own what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: fully responsible for the ethical use of GenAI and the appropriateness, accuracy and originality

units.why: "must consider the ethical implications ... including potential biases, misinformation, limitations" asks students to weigh bias and harms (P53).
units.anchor: must consider the ethical implications of using GenAI tools in their coursework, including potential biases

units.why: The same sentence names "data privacy, and intellectual property rights" as considerations; coded P52 for the IP part, kept apart from the bias unit because it is a distinct concern.
units.anchor: information security, data privacy, and intellectual property rights

units.why: "must avoid inputting sensitive information such as university-specific, confidential, or personal data into external AI platforms" is a data-protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: must avoid inputting sensitive information such as university-specific, confidential, or personal data

units.why: "students should discuss with their instructors if they have any concerns about equitable access to the tool" is an equity-and-access provision (P51).
units.anchor: students should discuss with their instructors if they have any concerns about equitable access
units.frag_start: In instances where an AI tool

units.why: "Students are encouraged to explore the use of AI tools" welcomes AI use, a default-encouraging statement (P02).
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to explore the use of AI tools

units.why: "complement or enhance their skills rather than replace their own critical thinking" keeps the student as the thinker (P32).
units.anchor: complement or enhance their skills rather than replace their own critical thinking or intellectual growth

units.why: "understand the basis and limitations of AI-generated content rather than simply accepting it" is a verify-and-evaluate duty (P31).
units.anchor: understand the basis and limitations of AI-generated content rather than simply accepting it

units.why: "a course instructor has complete autonomy in determining the pedagogical use of GenAI tools" hands the decision to instructors (P04).
units.anchor: a course instructor has complete autonomy in determining the pedagogical use of GenAI tools
units.frag_start: The Florida Institute of Technology acknowledges

units.why: "must ensure students have equitable access to the respective tool or the assignments can be completed using a free version" binds instructors who adopt AI to keep access equitable (P51).
units.anchor: must ensure students have equitable access to the respective tool

units.why: "Instructors are required to incorporate a course policy statement into their course syllabi" is the syllabus-statement mandate (P09).
units.anchor: required to incorporate a course policy statement into their course syllabi

units.why: "The course syllabus must clearly state whether the use of GenAI tools in coursework is allowed" restates the mandate with required content (P09); kept as a distinct requirement about clarity of allowed or prohibited.
units.anchor: must clearly state whether the use of GenAI tools in coursework is allowed

units.why: Three sample statements named "Option 1: Open Use", "Option 2: Restricted Use" and "Option 3: Prohibited Use" are named tiers (P05); this is why the document stance is delegates.
units.anchor: Option 2: Restricted Use
units.policy: The guideline offers three sample syllabus statements: Open Use, Restricted Use and Prohibited Use.

units.why: The Open Use sample says students "are permitted to use generative AI (GenAI) technologies for brainstorming, research assistance, and writing support", a permission for brainstorming among other uses (P15; the tier itself is P05).
units.anchor: permitted to use generative AI (GenAI) technologies for brainstorming, research assistance, and writing support

units.why: Open Use sample: "all use of GenAI must be clearly disclosed" is a disclosure duty (P24).
units.anchor: all use of GenAI must be clearly disclosed

units.why: Open Use sample: GenAI "not replace original thought or fundamental skills such as critical thinking" keeps students as primary thinker (P32).

units.anchor: specific instructions for particular assignments will be communicated to students as necessary

units.why: Open Use sample: students "are not permitted to use GenAI ... in a way that would violate the Academic Honesty Policy" ties use to misconduct rules (P36).
units.anchor: not permitted to use GenAI in their academic work in a way that would violate

units.why: Restricted Use sample: GenAI "is permitted in this course under specific conditions" for listed purposes, a narrow permission tier (P05).
units.anchor: is permitted in this course under specific conditions

units.why: Restricted Use sample: "the use of generative AI tools is NOT allowed for" listed uses such as full essays, problem sets and code generation, banning AI-produced submitted work (P19).
units.anchor: the use of generative AI tools is NOT allowed for

units.why: Restricted Use sample: "All GenAI use must be explicitly disclosed in submitted work" (P24).
units.anchor: All GenAI use must be explicitly disclosed in submitted work

units.why: Restricted Use sample: failing the guidelines "will be considered a violation of academic integrity" (P36).
units.anchor: Failure to follow these guidelines or using GenAI in a manner that violates the

units.anchor: should be used to enhance understanding and creativity, not replace original thought or fundamental skills

units.anchor: please consult your instructor for clarification and guidance

units.anchor: the use of generative AI tools is NOT permitted for any assignments in this course

units.why: Prohibited Use sample opens with "To ensure the development of critical skills", the reason offered for banning AI (P41).

units.why: Prohibited Use sample: "All work must be completed independently by the student" requires submitted work to be the student's own (P29).

units.why: The disclosure templates ask for "[type name of the specific generative AI tool(s), version #, access date]", so disclosure names tool, version and date (P25).
units.anchor: type name of the specific generative AI tool(s), version #, access date

units.why: General Disclosure Statement says "I (or my team) reviewed, validated, and edited all AI-generated content", an attestation of verification (P31).
units.anchor: reviewed, validated, and edited all AI-generated content included in the submitted work

units.why: Code Generation Support template: AI used "to generate the basic framework of this code", then reviewed and modified, shows AI-generated code allowed with disclosure and review (P16).
units.anchor: to generate the basic framework of this code

units.why: Writing Support template covers AI "for grammatical corrections, sentence structure, and vocabulary suggestions", a prose-specific use (P18).
units.anchor: for grammatical corrections, sentence structure, and vocabulary suggestions

units.why: Brainstorming Support template: AI "to generate initial ideas for this assignment" (P15).
units.anchor: to generate initial ideas for this assignment

units.why: Problem-solving Support template: AI "to enhance my (our) understanding of" a class concept is tutor-like concept help (P12).
units.anchor: to enhance my (our) understanding of

units.why: Resource Assistance template: AI "to help identify relevant resources" with information "independently verified", a permitted research use (P14 not fitting; chose P31 because the statement stresses verifying output).
units.anchor: All information has been independently verified by me (or my team) for accuracy

units.why: Citation Assistance template: AI "to format and/or organize references", a writing-support use (P18).
units.anchor: to format and/or organize references in this assignment

units.why: The page lists "Florida Tech Licensed Generative AI Tools", Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini, with university-account login, sanctioned tools (P17).
units.anchor: Log in using your Florida Tech Microsoft account

units.why: "Access is limited to the web browser only. Mobile app and Windows OS integration are not included under our current license" states the scope of the licensed Copilot (P17; P07 not used since it does not set a student rule about built-in AI).
units.anchor: Access is limited to the web browser only.

documents.title: Student Academic Honesty Policy (Unauthorized Use of GenAI Tools section)
documents.summary: The university academic honesty policy contains a short section naming unauthorized GenAI use as a violation. It points students to the provost guideline and tells them to ask instructors.
documents.stance_why: The section says "Unauthorized use of generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in coursework constitutes a violation", so AI is barred unless authorized, which is restrict.

units.why: "Unauthorized use of generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in coursework constitutes a violation of the Student Academic Honesty Policy" classes unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Unauthorized use of generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in coursework constitutes a violation

units.why: "must align with the university's commitment to academic integrity, ethical standards, and the development of essential learning skills" is a principle for AI use (P56).
units.anchor: must align with the university’s commitment to academic integrity, ethical standards
units.frag_start: The use of GenAI within the University

units.why: Students "must consult their instructors if they have any questions about the acceptable use" of AI is the ask-first rule (P10).
units.anchor: must consult their instructors if they have any questions about the acceptable use

notes: Honesty policy coded only for its GenAI paragraph. Topic codes are my own slugs because AGENT_BRIEF.md was not available. The Syllabus Template link and the references list of AI tools were not coded.
